1	# webERP overall system
2	
3	webERP is a PHP and MySQL/MariaDB business application covering sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, finance and reporting. Browser pages and an XML-RPC API read and write one database through `DB_query`. The system hands work to SMTP mail, FTP, the Nominatim geocoder, Dompdf, shell build tools, `composer` and `phpunit`. Work comes in from users, cron URLs, CSV and bank-statement uploads, and EDI files.
4	
5	## Areas
6	
7	- **webERP database installation and upgrade**: creates the database and moves it between versions through three mechanisms:
8	
9	  - the installer's seed data and tables;
10	
11	  - legacy per-version SQL run by `UpgradeDatabase.php`;
12	
13	  - numbered PHP updates run by `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php`.
14	
15	  It takes redirects from `includes/session.php`, `includes/GetConfig.php` and the installer wizard. It writes the application tables, `config.DBUpdateNumber` and `config.VersionNumber`.
16	
17	- **webERP finance and ledger area**: the accounting core. It posts receipts, payments, journals, credit notes, depreciation and petty cash into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`.
18	
19	  - `gltotals` is kept in step with `gltrans` only by three database triggers. Every GL report reads it, including the trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and account inquiry.
20	
21	  - Apart from update `17.php`, the only code that writes `gltotals` directly is an INSERT in `DateFunctions.php` (line 1221) (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`, `source/webERP/includes/InstallFunctions.php:735-756`).
22	
23	  - It takes customer and supplier selection and stock and order work from the transactional area, and hands work to PDF and allocation pages.
24	
25	## Cross-area flows
26	
27	1. The installer area's wizard creates the database, folder, config file, tables, triggers and seed data.
28	
29	1. A page request reaches `includes/session.php` or `GetConfig.php`. These redirect to the upgrade area when `DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` or `VersionNumber` is missing.
30	
31	   - `DBVersion` is the highest available update file. It is worked out once at session start and cached for the rest of the session, so the check compares against that cached value and not against the files on disk. A comment marks this as deliberate (`source/webERP/includes/session.php:272-293`).
32	
33	   - A deployment made while users are logged in does not redirect them. Their sessions run the new code against the old schema, including features that `session.php` gates on `DBUpdateNumber` thresholds, until someone starts a new session and is sent to the upgrade.
34	
35	## Conventions
36	
37	- **GL balance check**: most posting pages call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, but at different points.
38	
39	  - Just before the commit: `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the finance receipt batch, among others.
40	
41	  - After the commit: `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`.
42	
43	  - Mid-transaction: `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main supplier posting.
44	
45	  - Not at all: `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php`.
46	
47	  - Some finance pages keep their own tolerance copies.
48	
49	- **Transactions**: most posting paths show no rollback or error handling, and failed queries are counted or ignored. The exceptions that roll back are the customer allocation pages, the CSV GL import, the customer receipt batch and the legacy upgrade helpers' per-step reporting.
50	
51	- **Upgrade errors**: the legacy runner and the numbered runner both continue after errors.
52	
53	  - **Scope of the guard**: `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` sets the `Errors` counter once per run, not once per file (lines 123-127). The `Errors == 0` guard therefore means "nothing in this run has failed so far", not "this update worked".
54	
55	  - **Effect of a failure**: once any update fails, every later guarded update skips `UpdateDBNo`, even if it succeeded. An unguarded update after that moves `DBUpdateNumber` past all of them (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:121-139`).
56	
57	  - **Reruns**: the next run starts at `DBUpdateNumber`+1 and repeats the updates that already succeeded. This is safe only if they are idempotent. `3.php` is not: it runs a raw `INSERT INTO tags VALUES(0,'None')` and `INSERT INTO gltags SELECT … FROM gltrans`, then `DropColumn('tag','gltrans')`, so a rerun fails once the column is gone (`source/webERP/sql/updates/3.php:3-29`).
58	
59	  - **The rule**: issue #304 set the rule that every update file checks `Errors` before calling `UpdateDBNo`.
60	
61	    - Files 0–16, 25–35 and 43 follow it.
62	
63	    - Files 17–24 and 36–42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally. That is seven of the last eight files, and no comment or script says this was deliberate, so a copy of a recent file will drop the guard (`source/webERP/sql/updates/36.php:4-5`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/42.php:10-11`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/43.php:310-312`).
64	
65	    - `17.php`, `19.php` and `20.php` increment `Errors` themselves and then record the update anyway (`source/webERP/sql/updates/19.php:6-12`).
66	
67	    - The runner has a @todo to move `UpdateDBNo` into the loop, and it has not been done (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:136-137`).
68	
69	## Hazards
70	
71	- Schema changes must be made in four places:
72	
73	  - the update files;
74	
75	  - the install tables and seed data;
76	
77	  - the install triggers in `install/sql/triggers/`;
78	
79	  - the legacy SQL.
80	
81	  Nothing compares them. Fresh installs miss anything added only to an update, and the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install.
82	
83	  - **Unguarded files**: any unguarded file after the failure moves `DBUpdateNumber` past it.
84	
85	  - **Counter reset in `17.php`**: `17.php` sets `$_SESSION['Updates']['Errors']` and `['Successes']` back to 0 partway through a run (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:21-22`). In any run that crosses update 17, the errors from every earlier update in that run are lost.
86	
87	  - **Effect of the reset**: guarded updates after 17 still call `UpdateDBNo`, `DBUpdateNumber` moves past the failed update, and the results screen shows 0 errors for it. This happens even when no unguarded file follows (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:120-158`, `source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:750-755`).
88	
89	- `38.php` calls `CreateTable('auditscript', …)` with SQL that creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/sql/updates/38.php:3-16`).
90	
91	  - **Broken existence check**: `CreateTable` checks `SHOW TABLES … ='auditscript'`, which never matches (`source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:518-534`).
92	
93	  - **Reruns fail**: on any rerun the CREATE fails because `auditscripts` already exists. Reruns follow an unrecorded update or a manual `DBUpdateNumber` reset, which is the workaround in issues #311, #760 and #811. The failure raises `Errors`, so every later guarded update in that run (for example 43) does not record.
94	
95	  - **Related names**: the install table file is named `auditscript.sql` but creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/install/sql/tables/auditscript.sql:1-9`). `LoginFunctions.php` purges `auditscripts` unconditionally (`source/webERP/includes/LoginFunctions.php:189-192`).
96	
97	- `gltotals` can drift from `gltrans` after update 17.
98	
99	  - **What 17 does**: `17.php` drops the three `gltotals` triggers, rebuilds the totals row by row, recreates the triggers without checking for errors, and records the update unconditionally (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`).
100	
101	  - **Failed trigger creation**: if `CREATE TRIGGER` fails, for example because the database user lacks the TRIGGER privilege, the upgrade still reports success. From then on, every GL report silently diverges from `gltrans`.
102	
103	  - **Writes during the gap**: any `gltrans` write made between the DROP and the CREATE is also left out of the totals.
104	
105	- Partial postings stay committed.
106	
107	  - Rollback from `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` is followed by autocommit writes, and no caller stops after it.
108	
109	  - Its rounding fix lands on the first row returned, not the largest line.
110	
111	- EDI invoices and orders can be resent or duplicated. Enabling `ediinvoices` on an existing customer sends the full history.
112	
113	- The release and CI checks are weak:
114	
115	  - The release check validates the previous `demo.sql` and passes when it is missing.
116	
117	  - `check_syntax.sh` cannot fail the release.
118	
119	  - `dump_database.sh` truncates the audit trail of the default `weberpdemo` database.
120	
121	  - CI tests only the Demo=Yes install.
122	
123	## Children
124	
125	- [webERP database installation and upgrade](weberp-database-installation-and-upgrade-149/brief.md) — This area covers how a webERP database comes into existence and moves between versions.
126	- [webERP installer, seed data, schema, build/CI and project-history area](weberp-installer-seed-data-schema-build-ci-and-project-histo-150/brief.md) — This area installs a fresh webERP database and company, supplies the SQL and seed data it loads, and builds, tests and releases the result.
127	- [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) — This area is the webERP PHP application.
128	- [webERP finance and ledger area](weberp-finance-and-ledger-area-152/brief.md) — This area is the accounting core of webERP.
129	- [webERP report writer, printable reports and report/admin pages: area overview](weberp-report-writer-printable-reports-and-report-admin-page-153/brief.md) — This area is webERP's reporting and print layer.

- **webERP finance and ledger area**: the accounting core. It posts receipts, payments, journals, credit notes, depreciation and petty cash into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`.

  - `gltotals` is kept in step with `gltrans` only by three database triggers. Every GL report reads it, including the trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and account inquiry.

  - Apart from update `17.php`, the only code that writes `gltotals` directly is an INSERT in `DateFunctions.php` (line 1221) (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:10-90`, `source/webERP/includes/InstallFunctions.php:735-756`).

  - It takes customer and supplier selection and stock and order work from the transactional area, and hands work to PDF and allocation pages.

## Cross-area flows

1. The installer area's wizard creates the database, folder, config file, tables, triggers and seed data.

1. A page request reaches `includes/session.php` or `GetConfig.php`. These redirect to the upgrade area when `DBVersion > DBUpdateNumber` or `VersionNumber` is missing.

   - `DBVersion` is the highest available update file. It is worked out once at session start and cached for the rest of the session, so the check compares against that cached value and not against the files on disk. A comment marks this as deliberate (`source/webERP/includes/session.php:272-293`).

   - A deployment made while users are logged in does not redirect them. Their sessions run the new code against the old schema, including features that `session.php` gates on `DBUpdateNumber` thresholds, until someone starts a new session and is sent to the upgrade.

- **GL balance check**: most posting pages call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, but at different points.

  - Just before the commit: `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the finance receipt batch, among others.

  - After the commit: `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`.

  - Mid-transaction: `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main supplier posting.

  - Not at all: `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php`.

  - Some finance pages keep their own tolerance copies.

- **Upgrade errors**: the legacy runner and the numbered runner both continue after errors.

  - **Scope of the guard**: `Z_UpgradeDatabase.php` sets the `Errors` counter once per run, not once per file (lines 123-127). The `Errors == 0` guard therefore means "nothing in this run has failed so far", not "this update worked".

  - **Effect of a failure**: once any update fails, every later guarded update skips `UpdateDBNo`, even if it succeeded. An unguarded update after that moves `DBUpdateNumber` past all of them (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:121-139`).

  - **Reruns**: the next run starts at `DBUpdateNumber`+1 and repeats the updates that already succeeded. This is safe only if they are idempotent. `3.php` is not: it runs a raw `INSERT INTO tags VALUES(0,'None')` and `INSERT INTO gltags SELECT … FROM gltrans`, then `DropColumn('tag','gltrans')`, so a rerun fails once the column is gone (`source/webERP/sql/updates/3.php:3-29`).

  - **The rule**: issue #304 set the rule that every update file checks `Errors` before calling `UpdateDBNo`.

    - Files 0–16, 25–35 and 43 follow it.

    - Files 17–24 and 36–42 call `UpdateDBNo` unconditionally. That is seven of the last eight files, and no comment or script says this was deliberate, so a copy of a recent file will drop the guard (`source/webERP/sql/updates/36.php:4-5`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/42.php:10-11`, `source/webERP/sql/updates/43.php:310-312`).

    - `17.php`, `19.php` and `20.php` increment `Errors` themselves and then record the update anyway (`source/webERP/sql/updates/19.php:6-12`).

    - The runner has a @todo to move `UpdateDBNo` into the loop, and it has not been done (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:136-137`).

## Hazards

- Schema changes must be made in four places:

  - the update files;

  - the install tables and seed data;

  - the install triggers in `install/sql/triggers/`;

  - the legacy SQL.

  Nothing compares them. Fresh installs miss anything added only to an update, and the numbered runner never runs on a fresh install.

  - **Unguarded files**: any unguarded file after the failure moves `DBUpdateNumber` past it.

  - **Counter reset in `17.php`**: `17.php` sets `$_SESSION['Updates']['Errors']` and `['Successes']` back to 0 partway through a run (`source/webERP/sql/updates/17.php:21-22`). In any run that crosses update 17, the errors from every earlier update in that run are lost.

  - **Effect of the reset**: guarded updates after 17 still call `UpdateDBNo`, `DBUpdateNumber` moves past the failed update, and the results screen shows 0 errors for it. This happens even when no unguarded file follows (`source/webERP/Z_UpgradeDatabase.php:120-158`, `source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:750-755`).

- `38.php` calls `CreateTable('auditscript', …)` with SQL that creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/sql/updates/38.php:3-16`).

  - **Broken existence check**: `CreateTable` checks `SHOW TABLES … ='auditscript'`, which never matches (`source/webERP/includes/UpgradeDB_mysqli.php:518-534`).

  - **Reruns fail**: on any rerun the CREATE fails because `auditscripts` already exists. Reruns follow an unrecorded update or a manual `DBUpdateNumber` reset, which is the workaround in issues #311, #760 and #811. The failure raises `Errors`, so every later guarded update in that run (for example 43) does not record.

  - **Related names**: the install table file is named `auditscript.sql` but creates `auditscripts` (`source/webERP/install/sql/tables/auditscript.sql:1-9`). `LoginFunctions.php` purges `auditscripts` unconditionally (`source/webERP/includes/LoginFunctions.php:189-192`).

  - **Failed trigger creation**: if `CREATE TRIGGER` fails, for example because the database user lacks the TRIGGER privilege, the upgrade still reports success. From then on, every GL report silently diverges from `gltrans`.

  - **Writes during the gap**: any `gltrans` write made between the DROP and the CREATE is also left out of the totals.

  - The release check validates the previous `demo.sql` and passes when it is missing.

  - `check_syntax.sh` cannot fail the release.

  - `dump_database.sh` truncates the audit trail of the default `weberpdemo` database.

1	# Business Requirements Document: Credit Control
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| Prepared for | Finance Director |
6	| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
7	| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
8	| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |
9	
10	## 1. Purpose
11	
12	This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.
13	
14	The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.
15	
16	## 2. Background
17	
18	We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.
19	
20	Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:
21	
22	- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
23	- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
24	- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
25	- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
26	- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.
27	
28	We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.
29	
30	## 3. Stakeholders
31	
32	| Stakeholder | Interest |
33	|---|---|
34	| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
35	| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
36	| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
37	| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
38	| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
39	| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
40	| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
41	| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
42	| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |
43	
44	## 4. Scope
45	
46	### 4.1 In scope
47	
48	1. Periodic credit reviews of customers, recording the outcome, notes and the next review date.
49	2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
50	3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
51	4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
52	5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
53	6. Writing off bad debts.
54	7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
55	8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
56	9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
57	10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
58	11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
59	12. Updating the staff guide.
60	
61	### 4.2 Out of scope
62	
63	- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
64	- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).
65	- Changes to how customers pay us, or to cash allocation.
66	- Customer credit applications and account opening.
67	- Supplier (purchase ledger) side.
68	- Changes to price lists, discounts or sales commissions.
69	
70	## 5. Business Requirements
71	
72	### 5.1 Credit reviews
73	
74	- **BR-01** Credit control must be able to record a credit review against any customer. A review records the date, who did it, the outcome (for example: limit confirmed, limit raised, limit reduced, put on watch, put on stop), any new credit limit, free-text notes and the next review date.
75	- **BR-02** Every customer on account must have a next review date. New customers get one automatically when their account is opened, based on a standard review period set by Finance (we expect 12 months, and shorter for higher-risk customers).
76	- **BR-03** The full history of reviews for a customer must be kept and viewable. Past reviews cannot be changed or deleted.
77	- **BR-04** When a review changes the credit limit, the customer's limit must update as part of the review, so the limit and the reason for it are always recorded together.
78	
79	### 5.2 Stop and watch
80	
81	- **BR-05** Credit control must be able to put a customer on stop, with a reason, and take them off stop, with a reason. Each change records who did it and when.
82	- **BR-06** While a customer is on stop, no new orders may be accepted or released for them, by any route: the sales office, the web shop, electronic orders and standing monthly orders. Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
83	- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
84	- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.

91	- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. # Business Requirements Document: Credit Control

| | |
|---|---|
| Prepared for | Finance Director |
| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |

## 1. Purpose

This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.

The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.

## 2. Background

We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.

Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:

- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.

We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.

## 3. Stakeholders

| Stakeholder | Interest |
|---|---|
| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |

## 4. Scope

2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
6. Writing off bad debts.
7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
12. Updating the staff guide.

### 4.2 Out of scope

- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).

content.text: Let me read the key briefs from the map to understand the system architecture:

content.content:
1	# webERP finance and ledger area
2	
3	Part of the map whose overview is root.md.
4	
5	This area is the accounting core of webERP. It posts bank, receipt, payment, journal, credit-note, depreciation and petty-cash transactions into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`, and it maintains the GL master data and schema those postings rely on. It takes work from browser forms, uploaded bank and CSV files, and the XML-RPC API. It hands work onward to PDF and print pages and to allocation pages. Pages elsewhere supply customer and supplier selection, stock, sales-order and purchase-order work.
6	
7	## Flows
8	
9	**1. Bank statement import** (`ImportBankTrans.php`)
10	1. The user uploads a file. Files over 1 MB are refused. The `ImportFormat` of the chosen bank account selects a parser: MT940-SCB, MT940-ING or GIFTS. All three fill `$_SESSION['Statement']` and `$_SESSION['Trans']`. The SCB parser exits the page on an unknown currency. Malformed lines are skipped or mis-parsed.
11	2. The bank account is looked up by account number and currency. If it is not found, a message is shown and import is not allowed. Each line is then matched to an existing `banktrans` row by date, amount and account, which sets `BankTransID`.
12	3. `ImportBankTransAnalysis.php` assigns each line to a customer, a supplier or GL lines. It writes session data only.
13	4. On process, a non-default-currency statement needs an exchange rate other than 1. Analysed lines are posted:
14	   - customer receipts as type 12;
15	   - supplier payments as type 22;
16	   - GL-analysed lines as type 2 (receipts) or type 1 (payments), plus `banktrans`.
17	5. A line that is not analysed but matches an existing row is only marked cleared. A line that is neither is dropped silently, and the session is discarded.
18	6. No rollback is shown for failed inserts. Importing the same file twice re-inserts analysed lines.
19

21	1. `SelectCustomer.php` (elsewhere) links in. Items are added to a session batch. A change of currency discards the items.

# webERP finance and ledger area

Part of the map whose overview is root.md.

This area is the accounting core of webERP. It posts bank, receipt, payment, journal, credit-note, depreciation and petty-cash transactions into `gltrans`, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and `supptrans`, and it maintains the GL master data and schema those postings rely on. It takes work from browser forms, uploaded bank and CSV files, and the XML-RPC API. It hands work onward to PDF and print pages and to allocation pages. Pages elsewhere supply customer and supplier selection, stock, sales-order and purchase-order work.

## Flows

**1. Bank statement import** (`ImportBankTrans.php`)
1. The user uploads a file. Files over 1 MB are refused. The `ImportFormat` of the chosen bank account selects a parser: MT940-SCB, MT940-ING or GIFTS. All three fill `$_SESSION['Statement']` and `$_SESSION['Trans']`. The SCB parser exits the page on an unknown currency. Malformed lines are skipped or mis-parsed.
2. The bank account is looked up by account number and currency. If it is not found, a message is shown and import is not allowed. Each line is then matched to an existing `banktrans` row by date, amount and account, which sets `BankTransID`.
3. `ImportBankTransAnalysis.php` assigns each line to a customer, a supplier or GL lines. It writes session data only.
4. On process, a non-default-currency statement needs an exchange rate other than 1. Analysed lines are posted:
   - customer receipts as type 12;
   - supplier payments as type 22;
   - GL-analysed lines as type 2 (receipts) or type 1 (payments), plus `banktrans`.
5. A line that is not analysed but matches an existing row is only marked cleared. A line that is neither is dropped silently, and the session is discarded.
6. No rollback is shown for failed inserts. Importing the same file twice re-inserts analysed lines.

**2. Customer receipt batch** (`CustomerReceipt.php`)
1. `SelectCustomer.php` (elsewhere) links in. Items are added to a session batch. A change of currency discards the items.
2. `CommitBatch` begins a transaction. It writes `debtortrans` type 12 and updates `debtorsmaster`. It writes `gltrans` and `banktrans` only when `gllink_debtors=1`. A GL item whose account is another bank account also writes a transfer `banktrans` row.
3. `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs before the commit. If the imbalance exceeds the currency tolerance, it rolls the transaction back. It nudges the largest line for smaller differences.
4. The page links to `PDFReceipt.php` (elsewhere). The session batch is cleared only after success, so it can be committed twice.

**3. Supplier credit note** (`SupplierCredit.php`)
1. `SelectSupplier.php` (elsewhere) supplies the supplier. The page builds `SuppTrans` and redirects to line pages: `SuppCreditGRNs.php` and `SuppShiptChgs.php` (elsewhere), plus `SuppTransGLAnalysis.php`, `SuppContractChgs.php` and `SuppFixedAssetChgs.php`. These fill the session only.
2. On post, the total, date, reference and exchange rate are validated. Posting then runs in one transaction. The `gltrans` rows are type 21. It writes `supptrans`, `supptranstaxes`, GRN quantities, shipment charges, contract charges and asset changes. No rollback is shown, and results of inserts are unchecked.

**4. Manual postings** (`GLJournal.php`, `Payments.php`, `RegularPaymentsProcess.php`, `Z_ImportGLTransactions.php`)
- Each begins a transaction and takes a period from `GetPeriod`. Dates before `ProhibitPostingsBefore` are moved forward silently.
- `Payments.php` writes `supptrans` type 22, `suppallocs`, `banktrans` and GL rows. Cheque numbers are checked against `supptrans` only.
- Regular payments commit one payment at a time.
- Only the CSV import checks the total, and it rolls back the whole file on any error.
- `GLJournal.php` does not check that the journal balances.
- Every `gltrans` insert fires a trigger that updates `gltotals`. Deleting or updating a row with no `gltotals` row changes nothing and gives no error.

**5. Allocation** (`CustomerAllocations.php`, `SupplierAllocations.php`)
- The inquiry pages link in, `CustomerInquiry.php` and `SupplierInquiry.php` (the latter also holds the hold/release toggle). The allocation pages write `custallocns`/`suppallocs`, update `alloc` and `settled`, and post exchange-difference GL rows.
- The customer pages roll back on error. `SupplierAllocations.php` shows no rollback.
- The session `Alloc` is cleared afterwards, so a repeat gets "can not be processed again".

**6. Bank matching, reconciliation and currency**
- `BankMatching.php` sets `amountcleared` row by row, with no transaction.
- `BankReconciliation.php` posts a type 36 exchange-difference journal dated the last day of the previous month. There is no duplicate guard.
- `Currencies.php` commits a rate change, then calls the bank-account adjustment, which is not transactional. PR #845 removed the automatic revaluation at login.

**7. Depreciation and fixed assets**
- `FixedAssetDepreciation.php` posts type 44 monthly and updates `accumdepn`.
- `FixedAssetItems.php` posts types 42 (category change) and 43 (deletion).

**8. Petty cash**
- `PcAssignCashToTab.php` and `PcAssignCashTabToTab.php` record assignments as `ASSIGNCASH` rows.
- `PcAuthorizeCash.php` posts them to GL and `banktrans` and commits regardless of errors.
- `PcAuthorizeExpenses.php` posts claims with errors suppressed.

**9. API posting** (`api_debtortransactions.php`, `api_salesorders.php`)
- Receipts, credit notes and invoices from orders roll back only on the collected `$Errors`, so per-query failures can still commit.
- `InsertSalesInvoice` writes bookkeeping rows only.

## Hazards no part repairs
- Failed inserts mid-posting can leave partial data in the payment, credit-note, import, petty-cash and API paths.
- Reposting is not blocked: re-imported statements, double `CommitBatch` and double exchange-difference posts.
- Sign conventions differ between the SCB, ING and GIFTS parsers.
- `GetPeriod` creates periods without `gltotals` rows and shifts old dates.
- Division by a zero exchange rate is unguarded, and a rate of 0 is stored from missing feed data.
- Most pages lack permission checks and build SQL by concatenation.
- Pages with their own tolerance copies do not follow the `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` change.

## Children

These are in the folder weberp-finance-and-ledger-area-152/.

1	# webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API and install
2	
3	Part of the map whose overview is root.md.
4	
5	This area is the webERP PHP application. Browser pages and an XML-RPC API read and write one MySQL database through `DB_query`, with session carts holding work in progress. It hands work out to SMTP/mail, FTP, the Nominatim geocoder and Dompdf. Inbound work comes from users, cron URLs, CSV uploads and EDI files.
6	
7	## Flows
8	
9	**1. Sales order to invoice**
10	1. `SelectOrderItems.php` builds the session cart `Items<id>`. Each item goes through `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, which applies the price, discount matrix, zero-cost, credit-limit and duplicate-item checks.
11	2. `DeliveryDetails.php` validates addresses and freight, then inserts the sales order with a number from `GetNextTransNo(30)`. It can auto-create work orders and emails the factory manager. Failure: no handler or rollback is shown for the insert, and a duplicate POST creates a second order.
12	3. `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` checks negative stock and whether the order changed. Both checks exit before the transaction. It then posts the type 10 invoice (`debtortrans`, stock, GL, sales analysis, commission). `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs after commit, so its rollback comes too late to undo an unbalanced invoice (`ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php:1733-1734`).
13	4. `PrintCustTrans.php` renders the invoice. `EmailCustTrans.php` redirects to it with an address, and `PrintCustTrans.php` mails the PDF and deletes the file without checking the send. Pick lists go through `PickingLists.php`, with serial entry in `PickingListsControlled.php`. `GeneratePickingList.php` only prints.
14	5. Recurring orders: `RecurringSalesOrders.php` saves templates from the cart. `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php` (cron) creates the orders and, for dummy-item templates with `autoinvoice`, the invoices. Email goes after the commit. Only templates at locations the running user can update are processed.
15	
16	**2. Counter sale and return, credit notes**
17	- `CounterSales.php` creates the order, invoice and receipt in one transaction. `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs in the middle of it, so after an imbalance rollback the receipt GL, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and allocations are still written, with no invoice behind them (`CounterSales.php:1851-1900`). `CounterReturns.php` posts type 11 and type 12, requires the refund to equal the return total, and also calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` mid-transaction (`CounterReturns.php:1437-1580`).
18	- `SelectCreditItems.php` posts type 11 credits. `Credit_Invoice.php` credits an existing invoice and allocates the credit to it. Both call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit (`Credit_Invoice.php:1544-1548`). `CreditItemsControlled.php` collects serials for both. `Z_DeleteCreditNote.php`, `Z_DeleteInvoice.php` and `Z_DeleteSalesTransActions.php` reverse or wipe postings with no permission check.
19	- `Z_RebuildSalesAnalysis.php` truncates and rebuilds `salesanalysis`, discarding budget rows. If the INSERT fails the table stays empty.
20	
21	**3. Purchasing**
22	1. `PO_Header.php` and `PO_Items.php` create and edit POs. `PO_Items.php`, `PurchaseByPrefSupplier.php` and the auto-PO step in `SelectSalesOrder.php` create Pending POs, or Authorised ones when `authlevel` is strictly greater than the order value. `PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php` lists an order for approval when `authlevel` is greater than or equal to its value, so an order equal to the user's limit is created Pending and then approved by the same user. Its POST handler bulk-sets status with no value check and accepts any `Status<orderno>` key, so any order number can be set to any status (`PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php:17-26,69-94`).
23	2. `GoodsReceived.php` receives only POs with status Printed, which `PO_PDFPurchOrder.php` sets. It calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit. `SupplierInvoice.php` auto-receives only Authorised POs, and refuses any PO that has a controlled line. Its ReceivePO path calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit.
24	3. `SupplierInvoice.php` and `SupplierCredit.php` build `SuppTrans`. `SuppInvGRNs.php`, `SuppCreditGRNs.php`, `SuppShiptChgs.php`, `SuppContractChgs.php` and `SuppFixedAssetChgs.php` add lines. Posting is one transaction, but `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs in the middle of it (line 1469; commit at line 1858), not at the end. The `supptrans` insert and about 390 further lines of GRN and PO updates run after the check, and after any rollback it caused, in which case they are written in autocommit mode and the final commit commits nothing (`SupplierInvoice.php:1466-1495`).
25	4. `ReverseGRN.php` reverses a GRN. `Shipments.php` and `ShipmentCosting.php` cost and close shipments. `OffersReceived.php` turns accepted offers into Pending POs and mails the supplier. If `OffersReceived.php`'s mail group is empty it exits before rejected offers are processed.
26	
27	**4. Stock**
28	- `StockTransfers.php` moves stock immediately. `StockLocTransfer.php` writes `loctransfers`, and `StockLocTransferReceive.php` receives them with no rollback. Controlled lines use `StockTransferControlled.php`.
29	- `StockAdjustments.php` calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit, commits and then emails. It updates `stockserialitems` and `stockserialmoves` for controlled items (`StockAdjustments.php:248-280`). `StockCheck.php` freezes quantities, `StockCounts.php` records counts, and `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` posts adjustments and truncates the check tables after streaming. A repeat is only safe once the tables are empty. `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` changes `locstock` and `stockmoves` for every item but never touches `stockserialitems` or `stockserialmoves`, so for serial- or batch-controlled items a count adjustment leaves `locstock` out of step with the serial and batch quantities, and later picks, transfers and serial reports will not match on-hand stock. It also posts GL without calling `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` (`PDFStockCheckComparison.php:92-167`).
30	- Internal requests are raised in `InternalStockRequest.php`, authorised in `InternalStockRequestAuthorisation.php`, and issued in `InternalStockRequestFulfill.php`, one transaction per line.
31	- All serial and batch entry goes through `InputSerialItems.php`.
32	
33	**5. Work orders and BOM**
34	- `WorkOrderEntry.php` saves with no transaction. `WorkOrderIssue.php` issues material. `WorkOrderReceive.php` receives output and does not check `closed`. `WOSerialNos.php` manages serials. `WorkOrderCosting.php` closes the order, deletes its `woserialnos` rows, posts GL without calling `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, and has no guard against closing twice.
35	- `BOMs.php` and `BOMs_SingleLevel.php` maintain components and call `UpdateCost`. `CopyBOM.php` bypasses their recursion checks. `Z_BottomUpCosts.php` recosts from the leaves.
36	- Contracts: `Contracts.php` saves with no transaction and creates the quotation. `ContractCosting.php` closes at status 2. `SuppContractChgs.php` charges supplier invoices to contracts at status 2.
37	
38	**6. EDI and batch interfaces**
39	- `EDIProcessOrders.php` reads files and always creates the order, because `CreateOrder = true` is an assignment. Files are never removed, so a re-read duplicates the order. Its error email goes to the current user, not to the sysadmins queried.
40	- `EDISendInvoices.php` never sets `edisent`, because the update at line 211 is commented out, so each run resends everything. The Reece variant sets it at line 304. Whether that runs before or after the send is unverified. In both variants `edisent` defaults to 0, so enabling `ediinvoices` for an existing customer sends their whole invoice and credit history unless it is first set to 1 by hand (`EDISendInvoices.php:52-56,211`; `EDISendInvoices_Reece.php:13-15,304`).
41	- `FTP_RadioBeacon.php` uploads one order and flags it printed. `Z_ExportSalesAnalysis.php` runs unauthenticated and sends data to a hardcoded FTP server.
42	
43	## Hazards
44	- **Unescaped SQL:** SQL is built from request values on nearly every page.
45	- **Missing permission checks:** most pages show none, including destructive utilities and `PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php`.
46	- **No rollback:** most posting paths show none. Exceptions are `StockLocTransferReceive.php`, `WorkOrderIssue.php`, the supplier posting, and the tender save. They continue after failed queries, so partial postings can be committed.
47	- **Posting after commit:** `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` after commit cannot undo anything. Old-row deletes in `Z_Change*Code.php` also run after commit.
48	- **GL balance check placement:** callers put `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` in three different places, and each fails differently. `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` calls it after the commit, so a large imbalance stays in the ledger. `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the ReceivePO path in `SupplierInvoice.php` call it just before the commit. `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main `SupplierInvoice.php` posting call it mid-transaction. `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php` post GL without calling it. A new posting page copies one of these patterns.
49	- **Rollback without stop:** `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` does roll back on an imbalance, but it returns nothing and no caller stops. Everything the caller runs after the rollback is written with no transaction open, in autocommit mode, so the rollback itself produces a partial posting that stays committed. Mid-transaction callers are therefore worse off than the after-commit case. This assumes `DB_Txn_Rollback` issues a plain ROLLBACK with autocommit on, which `ConnectDB_mysqli` would confirm (`includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php:92-119`; `CounterSales.php:1851-1900`; `SupplierInvoice.php:1466-1495`).
50	- **Balancing fix hits the wrong line:** the automatic fix in `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` does not adjust the largest GL line. `SELECT counterindex, MAX(amount) … GROUP BY counterindex` returns one row per `counterindex` and the code takes the first, so the rounding difference lands on whichever row the database returns first, usually the lowest `counterindex`, such as the debtors control or a freight line (`includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php:105-115`).
51	- **No duplicate-submission guards:** orders, issues, receipts and adjustments can be doubled. Suppliers' `OffersReceived.php` accepts forged action keys.
52	- **Orphans and drift:** deletes with incomplete guards leave dangling rows. `Z_ChangeStockCategory.php` leaves GL posting rows on the old code. Location creates through the API lack `locstock` and `locationusers`.
53	- **Side effects on view:** `SelectCustomer.php` writes `custbranch.lat` and `lng` on view, and `Suppliers.php` overwrites good coordinates with 0 when a geocode fails.
54	- **Stored secrets:** SMTP, EDI and shop passwords are stored in plain text.

# webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API and install

Part of the map whose overview is root.md.

This area is the webERP PHP application. Browser pages and an XML-RPC API read and write one MySQL database through `DB_query`, with session carts holding work in progress. It hands work out to SMTP/mail, FTP, the Nominatim geocoder and Dompdf. Inbound work comes from users, cron URLs, CSV uploads and EDI files.

## Flows

**1. Sales order to invoice**
1. `SelectOrderItems.php` builds the session cart `Items<id>`. Each item goes through `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, which applies the price, discount matrix, zero-cost, credit-limit and duplicate-item checks.
2. `DeliveryDetails.php` validates addresses and freight, then inserts the sales order with a number from `GetNextTransNo(30)`. It can auto-create work orders and emails the factory manager. Failure: no handler or rollback is shown for the insert, and a duplicate POST creates a second order.
3. `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` checks negative stock and whether the order changed. Both checks exit before the transaction. It then posts the type 10 invoice (`debtortrans`, stock, GL, sales analysis, commission). `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs after commit, so its rollback comes too late to undo an unbalanced invoice (`ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php:1733-1734`).
4. `PrintCustTrans.php` renders the invoice. `EmailCustTrans.php` redirects to it with an address, and `PrintCustTrans.php` mails the PDF and deletes the file without checking the send. Pick lists go through `PickingLists.php`, with serial entry in `PickingListsControlled.php`. `GeneratePickingList.php` only prints.
5. Recurring orders: `RecurringSalesOrders.php` saves templates from the cart. `RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php` (cron) creates the orders and, for dummy-item templates with `autoinvoice`, the invoices. Email goes after the commit. Only templates at locations the running user can update are processed.

**2. Counter sale and return, credit notes**
- `CounterSales.php` creates the order, invoice and receipt in one transaction. `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs in the middle of it, so after an imbalance rollback the receipt GL, `banktrans`, `debtortrans` and allocations are still written, with no invoice behind them (`CounterSales.php:1851-1900`). `CounterReturns.php` posts type 11 and type 12, requires the refund to equal the return total, and also calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` mid-transaction (`CounterReturns.php:1437-1580`).
- `SelectCreditItems.php` posts type 11 credits. `Credit_Invoice.php` credits an existing invoice and allocates the credit to it. Both call `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit (`Credit_Invoice.php:1544-1548`). `CreditItemsControlled.php` collects serials for both. `Z_DeleteCreditNote.php`, `Z_DeleteInvoice.php` and `Z_DeleteSalesTransActions.php` reverse or wipe postings with no permission check.
- `Z_RebuildSalesAnalysis.php` truncates and rebuilds `salesanalysis`, discarding budget rows. If the INSERT fails the table stays empty.

**3. Purchasing**
1. `PO_Header.php` and `PO_Items.php` create and edit POs. `PO_Items.php`, `PurchaseByPrefSupplier.php` and the auto-PO step in `SelectSalesOrder.php` create Pending POs, or Authorised ones when `authlevel` is strictly greater than the order value. `PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php` lists an order for approval when `authlevel` is greater than or equal to its value, so an order equal to the user's limit is created Pending and then approved by the same user. Its POST handler bulk-sets status with no value check and accepts any `Status<orderno>` key, so any order number can be set to any status (`PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php:17-26,69-94`).
2. `GoodsReceived.php` receives only POs with status Printed, which `PO_PDFPurchOrder.php` sets. It calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit. `SupplierInvoice.php` auto-receives only Authorised POs, and refuses any PO that has a controlled line. Its ReceivePO path calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit.
3. `SupplierInvoice.php` and `SupplierCredit.php` build `SuppTrans`. `SuppInvGRNs.php`, `SuppCreditGRNs.php`, `SuppShiptChgs.php`, `SuppContractChgs.php` and `SuppFixedAssetChgs.php` add lines. Posting is one transaction, but `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` runs in the middle of it (line 1469; commit at line 1858), not at the end. The `supptrans` insert and about 390 further lines of GRN and PO updates run after the check, and after any rollback it caused, in which case they are written in autocommit mode and the final commit commits nothing (`SupplierInvoice.php:1466-1495`).
4. `ReverseGRN.php` reverses a GRN. `Shipments.php` and `ShipmentCosting.php` cost and close shipments. `OffersReceived.php` turns accepted offers into Pending POs and mails the supplier. If `OffersReceived.php`'s mail group is empty it exits before rejected offers are processed.

**4. Stock**
- `StockTransfers.php` moves stock immediately. `StockLocTransfer.php` writes `loctransfers`, and `StockLocTransferReceive.php` receives them with no rollback. Controlled lines use `StockTransferControlled.php`.
- `StockAdjustments.php` calls `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` just before the commit, commits and then emails. It updates `stockserialitems` and `stockserialmoves` for controlled items (`StockAdjustments.php:248-280`). `StockCheck.php` freezes quantities, `StockCounts.php` records counts, and `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` posts adjustments and truncates the check tables after streaming. A repeat is only safe once the tables are empty. `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` changes `locstock` and `stockmoves` for every item but never touches `stockserialitems` or `stockserialmoves`, so for serial- or batch-controlled items a count adjustment leaves `locstock` out of step with the serial and batch quantities, and later picks, transfers and serial reports will not match on-hand stock. It also posts GL without calling `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` (`PDFStockCheckComparison.php:92-167`).
- Internal requests are raised in `InternalStockRequest.php`, authorised in `InternalStockRequestAuthorisation.php`, and issued in `InternalStockRequestFulfill.php`, one transaction per line.
- All serial and batch entry goes through `InputSerialItems.php`.

**5. Work orders and BOM**
- `WorkOrderEntry.php` saves with no transaction. `WorkOrderIssue.php` issues material. `WorkOrderReceive.php` receives output and does not check `closed`. `WOSerialNos.php` manages serials. `WorkOrderCosting.php` closes the order, deletes its `woserialnos` rows, posts GL without calling `EnsureGLEntriesBalance`, and has no guard against closing twice.
- `BOMs.php` and `BOMs_SingleLevel.php` maintain components and call `UpdateCost`. `CopyBOM.php` bypasses their recursion checks. `Z_BottomUpCosts.php` recosts from the leaves.
- Contracts: `Contracts.php` saves with no transaction and creates the quotation. `ContractCosting.php` closes at status 2. `SuppContractChgs.php` charges supplier invoices to contracts at status 2.

**6. EDI and batch interfaces**
- `EDIProcessOrders.php` reads files and always creates the order, because `CreateOrder = true` is an assignment. Files are never removed, so a re-read duplicates the order. Its error email goes to the current user, not to the sysadmins queried.
- `EDISendInvoices.php` never sets `edisent`, because the update at line 211 is commented out, so each run resends everything. The Reece variant sets it at line 304. Whether that runs before or after the send is unverified. In both variants `edisent` defaults to 0, so enabling `ediinvoices` for an existing customer sends their whole invoice and credit history unless it is first set to 1 by hand (`EDISendInvoices.php:52-56,211`; `EDISendInvoices_Reece.php:13-15,304`).
- `FTP_RadioBeacon.php` uploads one order and flags it printed. `Z_ExportSalesAnalysis.php` runs unauthenticated and sends data to a hardcoded FTP server.

## Hazards
- **Unescaped SQL:** SQL is built from request values on nearly every page.
- **Missing permission checks:** most pages show none, including destructive utilities and `PO_AuthoriseMyOrders.php`.
- **No rollback:** most posting paths show none. Exceptions are `StockLocTransferReceive.php`, `WorkOrderIssue.php`, the supplier posting, and the tender save. They continue after failed queries, so partial postings can be committed.
- **Posting after commit:** `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` after commit cannot undo anything. Old-row deletes in `Z_Change*Code.php` also run after commit.
- **GL balance check placement:** callers put `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` in three different places, and each fails differently. `ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php` calls it after the commit, so a large imbalance stays in the ledger. `Credit_Invoice.php`, `SelectCreditItems.php`, `GoodsReceived.php`, `StockAdjustments.php` and the ReceivePO path in `SupplierInvoice.php` call it just before the commit. `CounterSales.php`, `CounterReturns.php` and the main `SupplierInvoice.php` posting call it mid-transaction. `PDFStockCheckComparison.php` and `WorkOrderCosting.php` post GL without calling it. A new posting page copies one of these patterns.
- **Rollback without stop:** `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` does roll back on an imbalance, but it returns nothing and no caller stops. Everything the caller runs after the rollback is written with no transaction open, in autocommit mode, so the rollback itself produces a partial posting that stays committed. Mid-transaction callers are therefore worse off than the after-commit case. This assumes `DB_Txn_Rollback` issues a plain ROLLBACK with autocommit on, which `ConnectDB_mysqli` would confirm (`includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php:92-119`; `CounterSales.php:1851-1900`; `SupplierInvoice.php:1466-1495`).
- **Balancing fix hits the wrong line:** the automatic fix in `EnsureGLEntriesBalance` does not adjust the largest GL line. `SELECT counterindex, MAX(amount) … GROUP BY counterindex` returns one row per `counterindex` and the code takes the first, so the rounding difference lands on whichever row the database returns first, usually the lowest `counterindex`, such as the debtors control or a freight line (`includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php:105-115`).
- **No duplicate-submission guards:** orders, issues, receipts and adjustments can be doubled. Suppliers' `OffersReceived.php` accepts forged action keys.
- **Orphans and drift:** deletes with incomplete guards leave dangling rows. `Z_ChangeStockCategory.php` leaves GL posting rows on the old code. Location creates through the API lack `locstock` and `locationusers`.
- **Side effects on view:** `SelectCustomer.php` writes `custbranch.lat` and `lng` on view, and `Suppliers.php` overwrites good coordinates with 0 when a geocode fails.
- **Stored secrets:** SMTP, EDI and shop passwords are stored in plain text.

## Children

These are in the folder weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/.

- [webERP credit notes: entry screen, posting, and delete utility…](weberp-credit-notes-entry-screen-posting-and-delete-utility-17/brief.md) — webERP/SelectCreditItems.php builds a manual credit note in the session.
- [webERP/ConfirmDispatchInvoice.php: confirm dispatch and create a sales invoice…](weberp-confirmdispatchinvoice-php-confirm-dispatch-and-creat-20/brief.md) — Loads an entered sales order into a session Cart, lets the user edit dispatch quantities, freight and taxes, then creates the invoice.
- [webERP EDI order intake, order-confirmation email and CSV export helper…](weberp-edi-order-intake-order-confirmation-email-and-csv-exp-24/brief.md) — webERP/EDIProcessOrders.php reads EANCOM ORDERS flat files from a directory, builds a sales order for each file and inserts it.

3	Part of [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.

5	This topic holds the sales order entry page `webERP/SelectOrderItems.php`, which is several fragments of one script. It loads or creates the session cart `$_SESSION['Items'.$identifier]`, selects the customer and branch, searches for items, adds them through quick entry, CSV upload and the frequently-ordered list, updates lines, applies discount matrix rates and cancels orders. It also holds three smaller pages: `OrderDetails.php` (a read-only order view), `InternalStockRequest.php` (an item list for internal stock requests) and `TopItems.php` (a report filter form).
6	
7	It takes work from browser GET/POST requests and from `DeliveryDetails.php`, which links back to it. It hands work to the cart class (`includes/DefineCartClass.php`), `includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, `includes/GetPrice.php`, and the database tables.

202	  10. `QtyInv > Quantity` -> warning 'You are attempting to make the quantity ordered a quantity less than has already been invoiced...The quantity delivered and invoiced cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
203	  11. A change is detected when any of these differ: `Quantity`, `Price`, `ABS(DiscountPercent-DiscountPercentage/100)>CurrencyTolerance`, `Narrative`, `ItemDue`, `POLine`.
204	  12. `CheckCreditLimits>0 AND AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit==false` -> `DifferenceInOrderValue=(Quantity*Price*(1-DiscountPercentage/100))-(old Quantity*old Price*(1-old DiscountPercent))`, subtracted from `CreditAvailable`.
205	      - `CheckCreditLimits==1 AND CreditAvailable<=0` -> warning 'The customer account will breach their credit limit', `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit=true`.
206	      - `CheckCreditLimits==2 AND CreditAvailable<=0` -> warning 'This change would put the customer over their credit limit and is prohibited', `WithinCreditLimit=false`, `CreditAvailable` restored, `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit=true`.
207	  13. `WithinCreditLimit AND Quantity>0` -> `update_cart_item(LineNumber, Quantity, Price, DiscountPercentage/100, Narrative, 'Yes', ItemDue, POLine, GPPercent, identifier)`. Otherwise it is skipped.
208	- A quantity of 0 is never applied through the update. The line stays at its old quantity, so it can be removed only with Delete.
209	
210	**Line display**
211	- `count(LineItems)>0` -> show the table, otherwise skip it.
212	- `DefaultPOLine==1` -> `ShowPOLine=1`.
213	- `OrderEntryDiscountPricing` token in `AllowedPageSecurityTokens` -> `ShowDiscountGP=2`. This shows Price, Discount and GPPercent as editable. Otherwise Price is read-only and Discount and GP% are hidden.
214	- `QOHatLoc<Quantity AND (MBflag=='B' OR MBflag=='M')` -> row background `#EEAABB`.
215	- `QtyRemain!=QtyOrdered` -> show the invoiced breakdown.
216	- `Some_Already_Delivered(line)` -> button text 'Clear Remaining', otherwise 'Delete'.
217	- `!Is_Date(ItemDue)` -> default date.
218	- `AllowOrderLineItemNarrative==1` -> show a narrative textarea.
219	- Sets `Items->total`, `totalVolume` and `totalWeight`.
220	
221	**OrderDetails.php**
222	1. Cast `OrderNumber` to int, include the session, and run the header query over `salesorders`, `debtorsmaster` and `currencies`.
223	2. `DB_num_rows($GetOrdHdrResult) == 1` -> show the header. Otherwise there is no output and no message.
224	3. `$CustomerLogin == 1 AND $MyRow['debtorno'] != $_SESSION['CustomerID']` -> error 'Your customer login will only allow you to view your own purchase orders', footer, exit.
225	4. Comments are exploded on ' Inv '. A numeric part becomes a link to `PrintCustTrans.php?FromTransNo=…&InvOrCredit=Invoice`.
226	5. `qtyinvoiced > 0` -> `DisplayActualDeliveryDate = ConvertSQLDate(actualdispatchdate)`. Otherwise it is `ConvertSQLDate(itemdue)` in a red span.
227	6. The line loop accumulates `OrderTotal`, `OrderTotalVolume` and `OrderTotalWeight`.
228	7. Zero line rows produce no message.
229	
230	**InternalStockRequest.php**
231	- No guards.
232	- A loop over `$SearchResult`. Each row fetches `GetQuantityOnHand(stockid, Request->Location)`, `GetDemand(stockid, Request->Location)` and `GetQuantityOnOrder(stockid,'ALL')`. `Available = QOH - DemandQty + OnOrder`.
233	- `$i==0` -> autofocus on the first input.
234	- `Quantity<i>` defaults to 0.
235	
236	**TopItems.php**
237	- `!isset($_POST['StockCat'])` -> `'All'`.
238	- The matching option is selected, or 'All'.
239	- The code for the PrintPDF and View handlers is not shown.
240	
241	## Decisions (summary of the key outcomes)
242	- Duplicate lines are rejected in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: `LineItems>0 AND SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` and `strcasecmp(StockID,NewItem)==0` -> message and the item is not added.
243	- Item not found in `stockmaster` joined to `locstock` for the cart location -> warn, not added.
244	- `discontinued==1` -> error 'Obsolete Item', footer, exit. That ends the whole page for any item in a batch.
245	- Zero-cost rule: an item is accepted if `AllowSalesOfZeroCostItems==true`. If it is false, it is accepted only for mbflag B or M with `standardcost>0`, or for mbflag A, D or K. Otherwise the message says no cost is set up.
246	- `ExistingOrder != 0` -> `UpdateDB='Yes'` and `NewLineNo = MAX(orderlineno)+1` (0 if null or <0). `ExistingOrder == 0` -> `UpdateDB='No'`, `NewLineNo=-1`.
247	- Discount in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`:
248	  - `MAX(discountrate)` over `quantitybreak < NewItemQty` (strictly less than).
249	  - The fragment above uses `<=`. A quantity equal to the break gets the discount in the fragment but not at first add.
250	  - Sell-through support rebates (`sellthroughsupport` by stock and by category) are added to `Discount`.
251	  - The rebate is converted at the currency rate when the currency differs from the company default.
252	- Credit check on add: `CheckCreditLimits>0 AND !AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` -> `CreditAvailable -= round(Qty*Price*(1-Discount), CurrDecimalPlaces)`. The value `1` warns; the value `2` sets `WithinCreditLimit=false` and the line is not added.
253	- `GetPrice` is called as `GetPrice(NewItem, DebtorNo, Branch, NewItemQty)`.
254	
255	## Order and failure
256	- Cancel deletes `salesorderdetails` first, then `salesorders`. There is no transaction and no handler, so an error after the first delete leaves a header without lines.
257	- Asset disposal runs `INSERT stockcategory`, then `INSERT stockmaster`, then `INSERT locstock`, then the add to cart. There is no transaction. A failure after the category insert leaves the category orphaned; a failure after the stockmaster insert leaves an item with no `locstock` rows.
258	- The asset id uniqueness loop increments `$j` until `ASSET-<id>[-j]` is free.
259	- `add_to_cart` builds the in-memory line first and then runs the INSERT (when `UpdateDB='Yes'`). A DB failure leaves a cart line that is not in the DB.
260	- `update_cart_item` updates memory first and then the DB.
261	- `remove_from_cart` raises `CreditAvailable` before it unsets the line.
262	- None of the pages has a handler around `DB_query`; errors go to `DB_query`'s own error handler. The one exception is `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, which shows a message on a DB error for the stock lookup.
263	- CSV upload has no file type, size or `fopen` error check. The loop `fgetcsv(..., 10000, ",")` runs per row.
264	- The credit check in the line update is not repeated per line once `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` is true.
265	- The default `identifier` is `date('U')`, so two orders opened in the same second share a session key.
266	
267	## Connections
268	
269	**`webERP/includes/DefineCartClass.php`**
270	- Methods called: `add_to_cart`, `update_cart_item`, `remove_from_cart`, `Some_Already_Delivered`, `Any_Already_Delivered`.
271	- `add_to_cart` returns 1 if `StockID` is non-empty and `Qty>0`, otherwise 0.
272	  - A negative Price becomes 0, and `LineNumber==-1` takes `LineCounter`.
273	  - It creates a `LineDetails` object and increments `ItemsOrdered`. With `UpdateDB='Yes'` it runs `INSERT INTO salesorderdetails`.
274	- `update_cart_item` has no guard. It changes the `LineItems` properties, and with `UpdateDB='Yes'` runs `UPDATE salesorderdetails`.
275	- `remove_from_cart`:
276	  - It refuses with an error if `LineNumber` is unset, empty or <0.
277	  - If `Some_Already_Delivered==0` it runs `DELETE` on `salesorderdetails`. Otherwise it runs `UPDATE salesorderdetails SET quantity=qtyinvoiced, completed=1`.
278	  - It raises `CreditAvailable` and unsets the line.
279	- `LineDetails` constructor:
280	  - `GPPercent = ((Prc*(1-Disc)-(StandardCost*ExRate))*100)/Prc` if `Prc>0`, else 0.
281	  - `QtyDispatched` is set from `InvoiceQuantityDefault`, but the code writes a mistyped property `QtyDispathced`.
282	- The `Cart` class also holds `GetTaxes($LineNumber)` and `GetFreightTaxes()`.
283	
284	**`webERP/includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`**
285	- Included per item from the quick-entry, asset and add-item paths. It holds the checks above.
286	- It calls `add_to_cart` and `GetPrice`.
287	
288	**`webERP/includes/GetPrice.php`**
289	- `GetPrice($StockID,$DebtorNo,$BranchCode,$OrderLineQty=1,$ReportZeroPrice=1)` returns the first price found, in this order:
290	  1. `prices` by the customer's salestype, `debtorno` and `branchcode`, date-valid.
291	  2. The same with `branchcode=''`.
292	  3. The same with `debtorno=''`.
293	  4. `prices` with `typeabbrev=$_SESSION['DefaultPriceList']` and `debtorno=''`.
294	  5. `max(pricematrix.price)` where `quantitybreak >= OrderLineQty`, matching currency and salestype.
295	  6. `pricematrix.price` by salestype and debtor.
296	  7. If nothing is found: `prnMsg('There are no prices set up for <StockID>','warn')` when `ReportZeroPrice==1`, and return 0.
297	- With a zero price the line is still added, since `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php` has no zero-price check.
298	
299	**`GetCustBranchDetails($identifier)`** (shown in this topic)
300	- Reads `custbranch` joined to `locations` by `Branch` and `DebtorNo`, and returns `$Result`.
301	- It has no error handling beyond `DB_query`.
302	
303	**`webERP/DeliveryDetails.php`**
304	- Both directions:
305	  - `DeliveryDetails.php` forwards to `SelectOrderItems.php` with `identifier` when `BackToLineDetails=='Modify Order Lines'`.
306	  - It links to `SelectOrderItems.php?identifier=…&NewOrder=Yes`.
307	  - SelectOrderItems.php redirects to `DeliveryDetails.php?identifier` on `DeliveryDetails`.
308	
309	**Other helper functions and tables**
310	- Functions: `GetQuantityOnHand`, `GetDemand`, `GetQuantityOnOrder`, `GetCreditAvailable`, `ConvertSQLDate`, `locale_number_format`, `filter_number_format`, `DateAdd`, `FormatDateForSQL`, `CurrencyTolerance`, `Is_Date`, `prnMsg` (behaviour not in this topic).
311	- Tables:
312	  - `salesorders`, `salesorderdetails` (read and write)
313	  - `stockmaster`, `locstock`, `stockcategory` (read and write)
314	  - `fixedassets`, `fixedassetcategories` (read)
315	  - `bom`, `discountmatrix`, `sellthroughsupport`, `currencies`, `custbranch`, `debtorsmaster`, `custitem`, `locations`, `locationusers`, `debtortype`, `holdreasons`, `salestypes`, `paymentterms`.
316	- `OrderDetails.php` links to `PrintCustTrans.php`.
317	
318	## Conclusions
319	- Quick entry, the asset path, and ordinary additions all go through `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`. They share its duplicate, obsolete, zero-cost and credit checks.
320	- Only the single-item and array paths expand kits in `SelectOrderItems.php`. A kit component then goes through the include, which looks up the component's own `mbflag`.
321	- `SelectingOrderItems` accepts only quantities `> 0`, so a zero or blank quantity is dropped silently.
322	- The credit check in the line update stops at `CheckCreditLimits==2` only for the line that breaches it. Other lines in the same post still run, with `CreditAvailable` restored.
323	- `ExistingOrder==0` (new order) lines exist only in the session until `DeliveryDetails.php` saves them (behaviour not in this topic). On an existing order every add, update and delete writes to `salesorderdetails` immediately.
324	- Cancel refuses only when some line has `qtyinvoiced > 0`. It does not check order status or authorisation, and it keeps no audit record.
325	- `$CustomerLogin`: on a modify load and in `OrderDetails.php`, a customer login sees only its own `debtorno`. Both load paths enforce this. In `OrderDetails.php` the check runs after the header query and before output.
326	- The salesman restriction applies on modify load and on customer selection. `OrderDetails.php` has no salesman check.
327	- `OrderDetails.php` only reads. Its `(int)` cast makes a non-numeric number 0, which yields an empty page.
328	- Customer selection does not check that the branch belongs to the debtor, and nothing guards a repeated selection.
329	- The same CSV or POST repeated adds the lines again, unless `SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` blocks the same stock id. For a CSV batch, the first duplicate prints a message for that item and the rest continue.
330	- The `<` versus `<=` difference above also means the quantity break is inclusive in the matrix re-application only.
331	- A discount-category line that is deleted or changed can leave other lines at the old matrix rate until the next matrix pass.
332	- `InternalStockRequest.php` and `TopItems.php` share no records with order entry except the `StockID`, location and category tables. They are separate pages; a change to order entry does not reach them.
333	- `GetQuantityOnHand` and `GetDemand` use the cart `Location` in order entry and `Request->Location` in `InternalStockRequest.php`. `GetQuantityOnOrder` always uses 'ALL'.
334	
335	## Hazards
336	- The CSRF `FormID` is only sent as a hidden field. The customer selection logic shows no validation of it.
337	- Search keywords, codes and customer ids are interpolated into SQL. The code shows no escaping apart from the `(int)` cast in `OrderDetails.php`, so injection is possible.
338	- `$_GET['Delete']` has no format check. `$identifier` is not validated.
339	- Partial failure in asset disposal and cancel (above).
340	- A division by a zero `Price` in the GP% calculation of the discount matrix pass is not guarded. The update path guards `Price!=0`.
341	- Input errors for `TopItems.php` after submit are not validated.
342	
343	## Connected topics
